conclusion: The image returns normally, but self-suspend and other API-masked intervals exceed twenty-five microseconds. CPU0 and other-core busy-wake maxima exceed the frozen nonregression predictions. Physical testing stops at this miss. This run does not qualify worst-case control-record cost or the task-wake percentile.
narrative:
Offline admission reports admitted: true for the same frozen ELF and session arguments on port 3-3 before submission. The ELF SHA-256 is d39edfe8e152d80d86ba796d77cffdf0596e2bf1ddf26921528546bbfe4de74a, compiled from clean revision 6076b12e. The queue git_revision identifies the runner, not the compiled scheduler. Return and rail restoration complete normally, with no native first failure. Native launch takes 6.303258 s and total host time is 24.094952 s, within the recorded budgets. All eight cores complete 64 idle and 128 busy samples; CPU0 retains 329 timer intervals with none dropped.

Self-suspension publishes its borrowed-lifetime atomic state before the kernel-added mask and drains no controls in its local transition or selection. Core 0 records reference 0.875 us, publication 5.083333 us, mask admission plus local commit 17 us, frame save 4.708333 us and C selection 13 us. The 34.708333 us field named masked_c_ticks starts before mask admission; it is an inclusive admission-to-C-marker interval, not a proven continuously masked interval. A matching core-1 exception enclosure resolves the boundary: reference and publication take 1.583333 and 5.083333 us, then 2.25 us elapses before the recorded mask begins. Masked local commit, frame save and selection take 8.208333, 4.625 and 18.583333 us, totaling 31.416667 us. Recorder finalization and port return add 15.583333 us, giving a 47 us recorded self-mask interval. Thus the target fails independently of the admission-label limitation. The local interval includes the EL0 mask SVC, observers, trace copying, guards and local stores; stamps do not isolate queue mutation. Selection includes constant-time choice, stack checking, dispatch publication and scanning, and continuation-SGI barriers. No hidden general drain occurs.

The repeated record is explained by the earlier maintenance wrapper, not a lost FIFO race: it calls ss_control_drain before and after object repair. ss_control_repair republishes the deferred slot between those scans, and neither shares a visited bitmap. The source at f4713e44 contains that sequence and the first diagnostic retains two visits to the self-suspend slot before its frame is saved. The current entry-wide bitmap excludes a republished slot; the record-revisit negative restores a fresh scan and fails the assertion that the same record must wait for a new maintenance epoch. A separate negative resets the batch budget and fails its sixteen-attempt assertion.

The longest control drain takes 49.541667 us and retains one record, slot 4: FIFO 2 us, body 39.291667 us, unlock event 3.083333 us and final lifetime/event work 2.625 us, totaling 47 us. Other retained records take 25.916667, 11.833333 and 7.666667 us. No retained drain repeats a slot or drops a record. Source and linked negative checks enforce sixteen distinct attempts per maintenance entry. conditions.capture_scope: saved-frame C selection, retained control body and CPU0 instrumented whole tick
conditions.pmu_profile: SUNSTONE_SCHED_PMU ON; legacy span PMU, accounting, result, IRQ counter, control phase, DMA and TLBI diagnostics OFF

conclusion: The native image returns normally with valid per-core PMU samples, complete writer shutdown and clock ratios consistent with the approved operating points. Both whole-tick banks exceed the 130 us prediction, so physical testing stops. All retained target samples have zero data and instruction TLB walks. Similar refill counts accompany substantially different durations; a uniform cost per cache line does not explain the remaining latency. The cause of the backend stalls remains unresolved.
narrative:
Normal ROM return and rail restoration complete in 24.307013 s; native launch takes 6.496558 s. All eight cores complete 64 idle and 128 busy wakes. The frozen ELF SHA-256 is 1a0b2809e2d25fcf5fb75c565d4126d2b1e243ebb9ad9ce1c3d30664cd7d5f01. Its source is clean revision b98baf28. Linked TCR 0x200803519 selects cached walks. The queue identifies runner revision 9a5b263c. Offline admission reports admitted: true for the frozen submission arguments before the single launch. An earlier offline check lacks the runner's newly required captured-word input and performs no USB access. That input refusal is recorded separately from the image findings.

All cores advertise six event counters and capability masks 0x3f for both event banks. Every retained sample has status OK, positive cycles and no overflow; all writers acknowledge shutdown before the complete snapshot. A row retains the maximum-cycle invocation for its core, component and bank. Its count records all completed invocations; its events describe only the retained invocation. Self-selection and control use the core's parity-selected bank. CPU0 alternates tick banks, completing 100 bank-zero and 99 bank-one invocations. Banks measure separate invocations. All retained nonblank windows report zero data and instruction TLB walks. CPU0 tick cycles divided by time give 1793.087 MHz, while core 6 control gives 1998.233 MHz. These agree with the approved 1794 and 2002 MHz points and exclude execution near the probe rate of 494 MHz. Clock status passes before and after the workload. Short empty-window references have fixed boundary skew and cannot measure the core clock.

The six A55 self-selection times are 15.791667, 7.791667, 3.916667, 12, 10.333333 and 3 us, each within the 20 us prediction. The eight control-body maxima are 10.75, 8.583333, 3.708333, 11.291667, 11.333333, 3.125, 20.375 and 11.541667 us, each within 40 us. CPU0 tick fails the 130 us prediction in both banks, at 165.916667 and 155.125 us. The comparison record, entry 1794489876020619006-e8b9b5d9, measures 127.041667 us inside the complete handler, 130.375 us for complete C dispatch and 115.541667 us after task readiness. The PMU covers the complete instrumented handler; the post-readiness figure covers less work. General selection, outside the self-selection prediction, reaches 31.666667 us on core 4: 56,683 cycles, 23 L1D refills, 38 L1I refills, 48 L2 refills and 35 attributable L3 refills.

Self-selection on core 0 takes 28,286 cycles and 15.791667 us, with 21 L1D, 17 L1I, 38 L2 and 20 L3 refills. Core 1 takes 13,904 cycles and 7.791667 us, with 20 L1D, seven L1I and 32 L2 refills, plus 12,002 backend-stall cycles. Core 2 takes 6,945 cycles and 3.916667 us, with 22 L1D, 12 L1I, 39 L2 and 16 L3 refills. Cores 0 and 2 have nearly equal L2 refill counts but a fourfold time difference. The comparison record reports selections of 13, 18.583333 and 7.875 us on these cores. Its timestamp interval includes trace-helper work that the PMU excludes. The time differences therefore cannot establish an isolated cached-walk benefit.

The core 0 control body takes 19,179 cycles and 10.75 us, with 17 L1D, 48 L1I, 80 L2 and 16 L3 refills. The comparison record reports a 39.291667 us body on core 0. Core 6 control reaches 40,714 cycles and 20.375 us, with 12 L1D, 77 L1I, 89 L2 and 100 attributable L3 refills. These event classes do not form a strict hierarchy of identical physical transactions. CPU0 tick bank zero takes 297,503 cycles, with 156 L1D, 70 L1I, 297 L2 and 252 L3 refills. Bank one takes 277,933 cycles, with 162 L1D, 64 L1I and 272 L2 refills. Its 208,112 backend-stall cycles account for 74.88 percent of that invocation's cycles. Attributable L3 refills do not directly count DRAM transactions. The refill counts and duration spread do not establish that every modeled line incurs a uniform 150 ns cost.

New PMU result stores occur after counter freeze. Existing control and tick latency observers remain inside their measured workloads. PMU setup and publication can delay task wake outside these windows. The whole-image CPU0 busy-wake maximum is 210.416667 us; task-lock wait reaches 9.791667 us. The aggregate core 0 mask maximum, 489.416667 us, begins before the scheduler running flag. The retained core 4 interval starts after that flag and takes 86.25 us against the 25 us budget. This diagnostic does not qualify startup, the 10 us task-wake percentile or repeatability. Physical testing stops at the timing miss without a retry, optimization, integration gate or landing.

Source and final-ELF audits find DSB followed by WFI in ordinary idle. They find no cache discard, TLB invalidation or core power-down on ordinary idle, suspend, selection or cross-core notification paths. Physical cache retention through WFI remains unqualified. The tick directly notifies eight latency-wake fixture tasks when their samples are due. Each task is pinned to a different core. All eight targets remain after the event-owner changes; thermal and supervisor deadline work moves to PPI27. Full decoded samples, per-core comparisons, endpoint audits and host checks are in the evidence paths.

image: sunstone-a733-os, empty application and pinned mimus
hypothesis: Production OS and mimus images built with the default diagnostic options contain no latency recorder, scheduler trace, scheduler PMU capture or restore-span instrumentation. Functional scheduler changes may alter code and state size.

conditions.scope: host-only production link and disassembly audit; no board access
conditions.toolchain: clang 21, cached lld 21, same pinned dependencies
conditions.configuration: SUNSTONE_A733_OS ON; BOARD_SUPERVISED ON; empty or mimus application; diagnostic defaults OFF; partitioned ON; idle pull default 0 (unlimited)

conclusion: The four matched native builds pass. Production excludes the new recorder, trace, PMU capture and restore-span implementation. Retained OS-core code grows by 9352 bytes in both configurations; different output alignment gives whole-image text changes of 8192 and 10240 bytes. Initialized data is unchanged.
narrative:
The baseline is ce0f9c13. The candidate merges that revision without conflict and changes only documentation after runtime revision 86a5f0fb. Both empty-application and mimus builds use the same pinned mimus revision 647aeb63 and engine bcaf39ff. The local mimus checkout has advanced beyond the source record, so the comparison uses a separate clean checkout of the recorded pin. Both sides use tools/configure.py with explicit Clang 21 compilers on first configuration, matching dependency paths and default diagnostic options. Each target builds with four jobs. No board session is launched.

The empty OS ELF text grows from 987276 to 995468 bytes; initialized data stays 3536 bytes. The full mimus ELF text grows from 1549600 to 1559840 bytes; initialized data stays 4248 bytes. Summing retained input sections from the sunstone-a733-os-core target excludes mimus and its engine. This OS-core text grows by 9352 bytes in each image, with no initialized-data change. Output-section alignment accounts for the different whole-image text deltas. The comparison artifact retains every symbol and section contribution.

Both images add the same 24 defined allocated symbols. The control symbols are ss_control_drain_excluding, ss_control_has_pending, ss_control_park_on, ss_control_refresh_suspension, ss_control_resume_isr, ss_control_suspend_current, ss_control_suspension, ss_control_wake_mask and ss_control_wake_on. Notification adds ss_notification_gate_try_begin and ss_notification_owner_wait. Local symbols are consume, hint, ssKernelAdminWait, ssKernelCancel, ssKernelControlPause, ssKernelControlPrepare, ssKernelNotificationWake, ssKernelPullIdle, ssKernelStaticAvailable, ssKernelTaskMask, ssKernelWaitCleanup, ssObjectIsrLeave and ssObjectRepairWait. The inventory includes functions that the compiler now emits out of line; symbol addition alone does not imply a new API.

The additional uninitialized state is functional scheduler state. ssKernelTasks grows by 16384 bytes, ssKernelControl by 6656 bytes, ssObjectRepairWait adds 8704 bytes and ssKernelAdminWait adds 136 bytes. Their sum is 31880 bytes; output alignment makes each ELF's BSS grow by 32768 bytes. None is a recorder buffer. Existing generic idle telemetry and a weak event-insertion test hook are present in both baseline and candidate; this branch does not introduce them.

Compile commands, link maps and symbol tables contain no recorder, trace, scheduler-PMU or restore-span source object or definition. They use the ordinary generated SMP ports rather than private latency ports. The independent audit finds no recorder calls in the context-switch, selection and notification paths. Its 178 linked scheduler, task and port functions contain no diagnostic counter instructions. Recursive graphs from ten roots retain only functional timer and deadline clocks plus a panic-path clock; the source review records indirect-call bindings. This host audit establishes production exclusion and code size.

hypothesis:
The native CPU-only latency cause image returns normally on port 3-3 at CPU-L 1794 MHz/1000 mV, CPU-B 2002 MHz/1050 mV and DRAM 2040 MHz, with cached EL1 table walks. All eight cores complete 64 idle and 128 busy wake samples. Every core's cycle counter is configured, frozen and free of overflow; the report holds a complete eight-target tick, all fifteen barrier cases with 64 samples each, 384 SGI sends observed by CPU1, and 256 completed round trips for the local reference and for the CPU0-CPU1 and CPU0-CPU6 pairs. CPU0's tick runs at 1794 MHz within ten percent.

The run separates two explanations of the tick's 75 percent backend stall. H1: lines owned by other cores migrate to CPU0 on each remote release; cost follows lines touched times transfer time. H2: a DSB after a GIC write (ICC_SGI1R_EL1) waits for that write to complete; cost follows the count of such barriers.

Predictions (cycles at 1794 MHz unless stated; H1 / H2):
- ISB alone and DSB ISH or SY alone, median: 10-60 / 10-60 (both).
- Store then DSB ISH or SY, median: 10-100 / 10-100 (both).
- SGI write then DSB ISH or SY, median: at most 300 / at least 500.
- Half round trip, CPU0-CPU1 and CPU0-CPU6, median: at least 300 each / 60-300 each.
- SGI segment per remote release (owner barrier through SGI write): at most 1,000 / at least 2,000.
- Release remainder per remote release (release minus SGI minus mask restoration): 10,000-30,000 / at most 5,000.
- Sum of SGI segments over the retained tick (releases and forced deadline-scan SGIs): at most 15 percent / at least 50 percent of the tick.
- CPU0's own release (no SGI): at most 5,000 under both.
- Whole retained tick: 200,000-330,000 cycles (110-185 us) under both; the capture hooks replace the earlier PMU observers.
A mixed result (for example SGI+DSB at least 500 cycles but SGI segments below 50 percent) is reported as such, with each hypothesis's share computed from the segments.

Time budget: host preparation 1 s, rails 5 s, reset 6 s, DRAM 3 s, launch 9 s (boot and clock readiness 2 s, workload as in the previous run 4.5 s, barrier benchmark at most 960 samples plus 384 SGI-delivery ticks at 1 kHz = 1.35 s, line exchange bounded at 0.25 s, return 1 s), capture 1 s, rail restoration 3 s: 28 s total, below finish_by 55 s and the 60 s session lifetime. The application deadline is 12 s with a 5 s return reserve. The controller publishes progress every 1 ms tick; the longest gap is the line exchange's bounded 250 ms spin, below the 1 s application progress window and the 3 s runner progress window. Each benchmark sample masks IRQs for under 2 us. One measuring run follows check admitted:true; any transport, native, counter-validity or decoder miss ends the stage without retry.
conclusion: Neither explanation dominates the busy tick. SGI segments, including their barriers, take 2.2 percent of the retained tick; a DSB after an SGI write costs about 430 extra cycles, but production orders its DSB before the write. One line transfer costs 142.5 cycles within the Cortex-A55 type and 153.5 cycles to a Cortex-A76, so 250 migrated lines would explain about 10 percent. The same releases cost about 2,600 cycles in the idle phase and 11,000 to 74,000 in the busy phase, CPU0's own release (no remote lines) costs most, and cost falls with release order. The stall follows eviction by the busy memory traffic and refills from DRAM, not line migration or barriers.

hypothesis:
The native CPU-only latency cause image returns normally on port 3-3 at CPU-L 1794 MHz/1000 mV, CPU-B 2002 MHz/1050 mV and DRAM 2040 MHz, with cached EL1 table walks. All eight cores complete 64 idle and 128 busy wake samples. Every core configures the cycle counter and event counters 0-4 (L1I refill 0x01, L1D refill 0x03, L2D refill 0x17, L3D refill 0x2a, backend stall 0x24), all five events are implemented in PMCEID0, and the report holds a complete eight-target tick, the barrier benchmark and both line-exchange pairs.

Hypothesis: busy-phase traffic evicts CPU0's tick working set between ticks, so each segment's refills equal the lines it touches first in the tick, and its cycles follow those refills at DRAM latency. The eight-core QEMU model's busy ticks (28 complete ticks) give the first-touch counts, excluding diagnostic hooks: local release 30 data and 82 instruction lines; remote releases 8-11 data and 0-11 instruction lines each; deadline scans 1-2 data and 0-4 instruction lines; outside the releases and scans 35 data (25 of them fixture) and 51 instruction lines; whole tick 141 data and 152 instruction lines. The diagnostic hooks add about 50 data and 40 instruction lines per tick.

Predictions (busy-phase means over complete ticks; ranges allow for the hooks and for whether event 0x17 includes instruction refills):
- Local release: L1I refill 70-120, L1D refill 25-60, L2D refill 30-170, L3D refill 25-170, cycles 50,000-110,000.
- Each remote release: L1I refill 0-20, L1D refill 8-30, L2D refill 8-50, L3D refill 5-50, cycles 8,000-35,000; its cycles per L2D refill within a factor of two of the local release's.
- Each deadline scan: at most 6 L2D refills and at most 5,000 cycles.
- Outside: L1I refill 40-100, L1D refill 35-110, L2D refill 35-200, cycles 40,000-130,000.
- Whole tick: L2D refill 200-450, L3D refill 150-450, backend stall at least 60 percent of cycles.
- Idle phase: each release has at most 10 L2D refills and at most 5,000 cycles.
Refuting outcomes: busy refills far above the first-touch counts (for example more than 300 L2D refills in the local release) mean the model misses a walk and the model is wrong; refills near the counts but under 300 cycles per refill mean eviction does not explain the cost.

Time budget: as in the previous cause run (entry 1794502169612799798-8aea3851, 26.3 s total, launch 7.6 s). The event reads add under 1 ms of run time, and the 147,456-byte output adds about 0.2 s of readback. Host preparation 1 s, rails 5 s, reset 6 s, DRAM 3 s, launch 9 s (boot and clock readiness 2 s, workload 4.5 s, barrier benchmark at most 1.35 s, line exchange bounded at 0.25 s, return 1 s), capture 1 s, rail restoration 3 s: 28 s total, below finish_by 55 s and the 60 s session lifetime. The controller publishes progress every 1 ms tick; the longest gap is the bounded 250 ms line exchange, below the 1 s application and 3 s runner progress windows. One measuring run follows check admitted:true; any transport, native, counter-validity or decoder miss ends the stage without retry.
conclusion: Busy-phase traffic evicts the tick's working set. A busy tick averages 314,510 cycles with 220 attributable L3 refills against 36,541 cycles and one L3 refill when idle, about 1,268 cycles per refill. Data refills per segment match the QEMU model's first-touch line counts (local release 36 L1D refills against 30 lines; remote releases 10 to 14 against 8 to 11). Instruction refills are lower than the first-touch counts (34 against 82 in the local release) because the streaming load leaves part of the code in L1I.
note: The runner recorded host-error because the decoder checked events 0x24 and 0x2a against PMCEID0; the image returned normally. The corrected decoder decodes the same output offline.
